answer.verdict: Not upstream-ready. The seq_cst queue (publish, sleeper Dekker, drain flag) does not lose wakeups, reuse a slot early, or free a CLUT out from under a running draw. The blocker is a cross-worker data race: every worker runs one primitive at once and TexturePageCache memcpys a whole 8KB page, but Submit never treats a primitive's own texture as overlapping its own frame/Z, and T8/T4 page stride is ceil while PageId floors, so odd buffer widths mark the wrong page.

facts.c: Submit on the EE thread, under m_mutex, is the only writer of m_published. The store of count+1 is seq_cst and happens after the Job is written. Workers acquire-load before reading the slot.

Sleeper Dekker is closed. WakeWorkers seq_cst-loads m_sleepers after the publish store and notifies under m_jobMutex only if nonzero. The worker locks, seq_cst-increments m_sleepers, then waits while re-reading m_published. Either the worker sees the new count in the predicate, or the submitter sees the sleeper and notifies. A notify that lands before wait is absorbed by the predicate.

Drain wakeup is closed. Waiter stores m_drainWaiting=true (seq_cst) then waits with an allDone predicate. Worker stores progress seq_cst, then loads the flag and notifies under m_jobMutex. If the worker misses the flag, the predicate still observes the progress store.

Batched wakes (every 16 jobs, plus every Wait) can leave 1..15 jobs undrawn while workers sleep. Readers (ReadVram, Snapshot, Present, Sync, Clear, local transfer, ConsumeLocalToHost) all Wait, which calls WakeWorkers. That is latency, not a lost draw.

Slot and CLUT lifetime hold for one generation. progress is stored only after DrawPrimitive returns. The generation bump and the deque collapse run only after every progress==target. deque push_back is what LoadClut uses when count!=0; collapse copies back() before clear. Workers set t_clut from the job immediately before the draw.

ABA: generation is the high 32 bits. A worker that still has local done=(G,c) and does not run until 2^32 drains have brought the published generation back to G will not reset and will consume the new generation from slot c. At the logged ~120 drains/s that is ~414 days; at the pre-14 ~60k/s storm it is ~20 h. Not reachable in the fight log.

No UAF on the job table in the single-host-thread schedule. ~GSCpuBackend only StopWorkers: sets m_stopWorkers, notifies, joins. It does not drain. WorkerLoop returns on the flag and drops whatever is still queued. m_vram is not freed there.

StopWorkers does not take m_mutex. A second host thread inside WaitForWorkers (which holds m_mutex and may be in m_idleCv.wait) can watch workers exit on the stop flag without storing target progress, then use the CV after ~GSCpuBackend returns.
DrawPrimitive is called with no try. An exception skips the progress store, std::terminate's the worker, and every later Wait blocks forever.
Initialize stores m_vram before ResetUnlocked's Wait. A second init swings the pointer while a worker can still be inside DrawPrimitive on the old pointer.

Each worker runs the same job over its own 16-row bands. CT32/Z32/CT24/T8H/T4HL/T4HH pages are 32 rows, so two bands share a page but not an 8-row block. Per-pixel frame/Z RMW stays on the row owner and stays in primitive order on that worker. The race vehicle is TexturePageCache::Resolve memcpy of the whole 8KB page.
Self-overlap is not tested. Queued write-vs-texture and queued read-vs-frame/Z drain. The primitive's own texture rect is marked only after that test, then the job is published to every worker.

PageId row stride is (bw*64)/pageWidth (floor). MakePageRect uses ceil via +pageWidth-1 and forces stride>=1. For page width 64 (CT32/CT24/CT16/CT16S/Z*/T8H/T4HL/T4HH) floor==ceil. For T8 and T4 (page 128 wide) an odd bw>=3 and a rect taller than one page-row marks base+2*row instead of base+row. Example: T8 bw=3, pixel (0,64) is page base+1 in PageId and base+2 in the mask.

extra=1 for a mid-page base matches the template address spill: block 0..31 plus block-table 0..31 is <2 pages of pixels for CT32, T8, and T4. It is conservative when the base is page-aligned, not a miss.
REPEAT and CLAMP wrap into 0..tw-1 / 0..th-1 before the load, and bilinear wraps u+1 the same way. The tracker marks that whole rectangle, so FST UVs outside tw/th are not a miss in modes 0 and 1.

REGION_CLAMP returns the clamp-register range (U bits 4/14, V bits 24/34), which can sit outside 0..tw/th. REGION_REPEAT returns (coord&min)|max, bounded by max .. (min|max), also outside that rectangle. Those pages are sampled and not marked.
If regionMin>regionMax, REGION_CLAMP collapses to regionMax (std::min(std::max(c,min),max)). A naive [min,max] rect is empty and would mark nothing.

Sprite v0>v1 is handled: Submit takes min/max of the vertices, DrawSprite swaps. Coverage is ceil(fx0)..ceil(fx1)-1; the mask is floor-1..ceil+1 intersected with scissor, a superset for in-range values. Same for triangle floor..ceil and for positive line/point int truncation.
Scissor x0>x1: clampInt returns lo, so DrawSprite can write x=scissor.x0, while MakePageRect returns empty when x1<x0 and marks no page.

PSMCT16S/Z16S use the 64x64 page grid; only the in-page block table differs. CT24, Z24, T8H, T4HL, T4HH use the CT32 64x32 grid (PageExtent and the MakePageRect default), so a 32-bit word shared with 8H/4HL/4HH is the same page and is caught. Z width is frame.fbw in both the mask and WritePixel.
zTouched matches this renderer, not a ZTE check. ZTST is TEST bits 17-18; ALWAYS is 1. ZTE bit 16 is ignored by WritePixel too, so the mask does not miss a Z read this renderer actually does.

CSM1 marks the 16x16 the loader reads (bw 1). CSM2 marks one row, x=cou*16 .. cou*16+255, y=cov, which is what LoadClutUnlocked reads. Both compare that rect to the write mask only. CPSM is CT16/CT16S/CT32/CT24, page width 64, so the odd-T8 stride bug does not apply.

Local->local (direction 2) and local->host (direction 1) take the direction!=0 drain, then copy on the EE thread. Host->local (0) does not drain in BeginTransfer; UploadImage checks the dest rect against both masks. Frame readback drains.

TEXFLUSH only bumps m_epoch and invalidates the EE cache. Queued jobs keep the epoch stamped at submit. A later sample of pages a queued draw writes still SampleConflict-drains, and that drain bumps epoch again before the new job is stamped.

Threads off: workers stay empty (count<2), Submit calls DrawPrimitive and returns, Wait returns immediately. UploadImage now calls m_texturePageCache.Invalidate() on every call, including the early returns (null data, 0 bytes, direction!=0), which the pre-14 function did not. That is the single-thread pixel-visible change.

The new test compares threads unset vs "4" for CT32 sprites (ZMSK=1<<32), a second T8 with tbw 2, CSM1 CT32 CLUT reloads, and TEXFLUSH around uploads. It does not draw a primitive that samples its own FBP, a region clamp, an odd T8/T4 bw, or destroy the GS with a non-empty queue.

GS_CPU_RELAX is _mm_pause via immintrin.h on x86/x64 only. Every other arch, including Vita ARM and Android arm64/armv7 and MSVC ARM64, calls std::this_thread::yield() inside the 2048- and 4096-iteration spins.
Vita links pthread explicitly. There is no find_package(Threads). std::thread was already in patch 09. Android links log and android, not pthread by name.

Fight numbers and 467/467 were not re-run here. Status states drains/s sample ~120, write ~90, upload ~300, clut ~19, and that screenshots match. Those runs do not exercise the self-overlap or odd-bw or region paths.

fix.change: Before: after building frame/z/texture, only AnyPages against the queued masks, then MarkPages and publish. After: run those two waits, then PageMask own{}; MarkPages(own, frame); MarkPages(own, z); if (AnyPages(own, texture)) { DrawPrimitive(batch); return; } then mark and publish. The EE thread's t_bandCount is 1, so the inline draw covers every row and never shares the page with a worker memcpy.

Before: stride = max((max(bw,1)*64 + pageWidth - 1)/pageWidth, 1) (ceil, at least 1). After: bw = max(bufferWidth,1); stride = (bw*64)/pageWidth; with no max(stride,1). Matches PageId at ps2_gs_memory.h:403. T8/T4 bw=3 then strides 1, so (0,64) stays on base+1. Stride 0 is valid for a sub-page buffer.

Before: textured rect is always (0,0)-(textureWidth-1, textureHeight-1). After: per axis, mode=(clamp>>shift)&3. Mode 0/1: keep 0..size-1. Mode 2 REGION_CLAMP: if min<=max mark [min,max], else mark [max,max] only (matches wrapTextureCoordinate:149). Mode 3 REGION_REPEAT: mark [max, min|max]. U from clamp bits 4 and 14, V from bits 24 and 34. Pass that rect to MakePageRect.

Before: ~GSCpuBackend calls StopWorkers, and WorkerLoop:891 returns without drawing the rest. After: take m_mutex, WaitForWorkersUnlocked(), then StopWorkers(). Delete the drop comment. VRAM is not released in this destructor, so the drain matches serial Submit. The mutex also stops a second host thread from waiting on m_idleCv while the CV is destroyed.

Before: t_clut=job.clut; DrawPrimitive(job.batch); ++done; progress.store. After: try { DrawPrimitive(job.batch); } catch (...) {} then always ++done, store progress, and notify if m_drainWaiting. Do not rethrow (that std::terminate's the worker and sticks every Wait).
Before: m_vram=vram; m_vramSize=vramSize; ResetUnlocked() which Waits. After: WaitForWorkersUnlocked() first, then assign m_vram and m_vramSize, then ResetUnlocked().

Before: m_texturePageCache.Invalidate() runs for every UploadImage, then the function may return without writing. Pre-14 UploadImage did not invalidate. After, to keep PS2X_GS_THREADS unset identical: move that Invalidate inside the !m_workers.empty() block next to ++m_epoch. If the stale one-page cache after an upload with no TEXFLUSH is kept on purpose as a bugfix, leave the line and say so in the PR; do not claim threads-off is unchanged.

Before: non-x86 GS_CPU_RELAX is std::this_thread::yield(). After: on __aarch64__/__arm__/_M_ARM/_M_ARM64 use asm volatile("yield" ::: "memory"); keep _mm_pause on x86; use a compiler barrier elsewhere. Do not yield inside the 2048/4096 spins.

Add serial-vs-4 cases that fail on the holes: one sprite with TBP==FBP and no second primitive; T8 tbw=3, 128x128, then a CT32 draw of the page PageId assigns to (0,64); REGION_CLAMP with max outside tw/th; destroy the GS without an extra Sync and compare VRAM. Keep ZMSK off for one Z-sample case.

Before: x1<x0 yields an empty PageRect while clampInt still draws scissor.x0 when x0>x1. After: if scissor.x0>scissor.x1 or y0>y1, mark the single pixel clampInt will draw, or skip the draw the same way. Low; illegal scissor.

Before: generation is (target>>32)+1 in the high 32 bits. After: keep a separate 64-bit generation, or stop the published word from aliasing a live worker's (gen,count). Only matters after 2^32 drains.

contra: Draining in ~GSCpuBackend contradicts docs/status.md:639 and the comment at gs_cpu_backend.cpp:891, which call dropping the queue intentional. The comment's reason (memory already gone) is not what the destructor does: it never frees m_vram.

Gating the UploadImage Invalidate restores pre-patch threads-off behavior and also keeps a stale one-page cache when the game uploads and samples with no TEXFLUSH. The new test always TEXFLUSHes (ps2_gs_tests.cpp:1936). 467/467 does not decide which behavior is wanted.

Serializing self-overlapping draws, and correcting odd T8/T4 strides, can raise the logs/fight_drains2 drain rate (~120 sample drains/s, 18-21 fps). Nothing read here shows whether Tekken emits those draws, so those logs are not evidence the holes are dead.
